title: On-call decision pathways and notification matrix
author: Priya Nair
body:
Overview
========

Purpose: This page defines deterministic decision pathways for first responders, the notification matrix for internal and customer communications, and a compact runbook for common latency/availability incidents affecting the Redwood serving surface. The goal is to reduce cognitive load during incidents and ensure consistent customer messaging.

Scope
-----
- Applies to incidents that affect Redwood-hosted inference (Redwood API), Dedicated pools, and Private deployments that report into the central incident bus.
- Covers severity classification, triage decision tree, escalation ladder, and message templates for status page updates and customer notifications.

Quick summary
-------------
- If an alert meets Sev0/Sev1 criteria (see SLOs), immediately follow the Decision Pathway A (pages 1–2).
- For performance degradations that are partial or region-scoped, use Decision Pathway B (cache/batching checks).
- Use the Notification Matrix (table) to determine who to loop in and which channels to post to.

Severity and thresholds
-----------------------
1) Sev0 (Critical outage):
   - Symptom: Global/major-region failure -- API returns >=50% errors for > 5 minutes OR console inaccessible and automated failovers failed.
   - Business impact: All customers affected, orders blocked, SLA breach imminent.
   - Target response: 5 min ack, bridge established, primary oncall in bridge within 10 minutes.

2) Sev1 (High impact):
   - Symptom: Significant latency or error spikes for a subset of traffic (P95 > 1s with error rate increase > 5%).
   - Business impact: Multiple customers degraded; potential SLA impact for Dedicated customers.
   - Target response: 15 min ack, remediation timeline published within 30 minutes.

3) Sev2 (Medium): degraded performance for small customer segment or non-critical feature regressions. Acknowledge within 1 hour.

4) Sev3 (Low): minor, non-urgent issues (documentation, small telemetry gaps). Handle in normal sprint.

SLOs referenced
--------------
- Redwood API P95 latency: 150 ms (global), P99: 400 ms.
- Error rate: <0.1% rolling 5m.
- Availability: 99.95% monthly for hosted tier (critical paths).
- Error budget: 0.05% monthly; SLO violation escalation triggers when remaining budget < 20%.

Decision pathways (flow)
-----------------------
Pathway A — Broad outage (Sev0/Sev1)
1. Alert triggers (monitoring: api-gateway-errors, serving-runtime-healthy).
2. Pager fires to primary oncall. Primary must acknowledge within page window. If not acknowledged, secondary auto-escales after 3 minutes.
3. Primary runs quick checklist:
   - Confirm scope (global vs region): check status page telemetry and CDN edge metrics.
   - Attempt immediate mitigation: scale up dedicated pool, trigger fallback model variant (model-fallback policy), or enable degraded-mode routing.
   - If mitigation fails in 10 minutes, open incident bridge (Zoom/MSTeams link) and notify Customer Success and Product.
4. Activate communication cadence per Notification Matrix below.

Pathway B — Performance regression (Sev1/Sev2)
1. Check for recent deploys (git tag, canary window), autoscaler events, and batch queue backpressure.
2. Run standard perf triage:
   - Check KV cache hit rates (kv-cache-proxy metrics).
   - Inspect serving-runtime CPU/GPU saturation and kernel queuing (runtime-metrics/gpu-*).
   - Evaluate prefix caching and continuous batching behavior.
3. If root cause is capacity, apply temporary scaling policy (scale up burst) and schedule follow-up for quantization/throughput tuning.
4. If root cause is model quality (inference producing errors), revert to previous model version and open a model-onboarding issue.

Decision tree (ASCII)
---------------------
Alert -> Is error rate > 10%? --yes--> Is region global? --yes--> Pathway A
                                
                                    --no--> Pathway B (region-scoped)
        |
        --no--> Is P95 > 2x baseline? --yes--> Pathway B
                                     --no--> Monitor and create Sev2 ticket

Responder roles and responsibilities
------------------------------------
- Primary oncall (platform): first responder, run triage checklist, activate bridge if needed.
- Secondary oncall: backup, remediation support, takes over bridge if primary absent.
- Service owner (team): deep troubleshooting, patch/deploy, RCA authoring.
- Incident commander (for Sev0/Sev1): appointed by primary in first 15 minutes; responsible for coordination and final messages.
- Communications lead (Customer Success + PR): crafts customer-facing messages for public status and high-profile customers.

Notification matrix (internal & customer channels)
--------------------------------------------------
Columns: severity | internal channels | status page | customer-notify | SLA customers (Dedicated/Private)
Sev0 | #incident-bridge, @pager escalation, leadership thread, Ops bridge | Public status: major outage, update every 15m | Customers with impacted routes: email + phone for platinum contracts within 20m | Open enterprise hotline, assign CSM 1:1 outreach
Sev1 | #oncall, #ops-updates, product-alerts | Status: degraded service, update every 30m | Email + support ticket to impacted customers; CSM informed within 60m | CSM-led proactive outreach within 2 hours
Sev2 | #team-oncall, optional bridge | Status: investigating, update every 4 hours | Ticket note; no outbound email unless requested | Ticket and scheduled follow-up
Sev3 | #team-channel | Not required | Internal ticket | N/A

(Example status page payloads included below)

Status page message templates
----------------------------
- Initial public status (Sev0):
  "Summary: Redwood API is experiencing a widespread outage affecting model generation and embeddings. Impact: Most customers in us-west & eu-west may see errors or timeouts. Current status: Engineers are investigating. Next update: within 15 minutes. Incident ID: INC-2028-042."

- Follow-up (30m):
  "Update: We have identified increased request queuing at the controller layer tied to a kernel scheduling regression. Mitigation: temporarily routed traffic to warm pools and scaled dedicated pools for high-traffic tenants. Customers on Dedicated will see reduced latency within ~10–20 minutes. Next update: 15 minutes."

Customer notification templates (email)
-------------------------------------
Subject: Redwood service incident (INC-2028-042) — summary and next steps

Body:
Hello <CustomerName>,

We are currently investigating an incident affecting Redwood inference in the <region>. Some requests may return errors or experience increased latency. Our engineers have identified a contributing factor and are actively mitigating. We will provide the next update by <time>. If this incident is impacting production-critical workflows, please reply to this email or contact your CSM directly at <CSM Email>.

We apologize for the disruption.
— Redwood Operations

Runbook: immediate checklist (first 30 minutes)
------------------------------------------------
1) Acknowledge on pager and post to #oncall with brief: "ACK INC-xxxx: scope, initial hypothesis, first mitigation action".
2) Confirm incident ID and create incident timeline entry (inc-db or incident-tracker).
3) Run scope commands:
   - curl -sS https://api.redwood.io/health || echo failure
   - kubectl -n runtime get pods --selector=app=serving-runtime -o wide
   - redis-cli HGETALL kv:cache:stats
4) If CPU/GPU queue depth > 85%: trigger horizontal scaling playbook (scaling script: infra/scale-dedicated.sh --burst)
5) If recent deploy within 30 minutes: rollback canary via deploy tool (ci/rollback --tag <previous>).
6) Start a live timeline and attach logs (s3://inc-logs/INC-xxxx).

Postmortem & RCA process (short)
--------------------------------
- Owner: service team. Due within 7 business days for Sev1+, 14 days for Sev2.
- Template to include: incident summary, timeline (minute-granular), root cause, contributing factors, corrective actions (owner + due date), and verification plan.
- Publish in Confluence under /incidents with tag incident-YYYY-MM-DD and link to incident artifacts.

Game day scenarios and cadence
-----------------------------
- Quarterly game days focusing on: KV cache stampede, model-fallback path validation, cross-region failover, and SLO-attack drill (sudden traffic spike simulation).
- Typical 4-hour game day schedule: 30m pre-brief, 2h scenario run with injects, 45m postmortem + 45m action planning.
- Success criteria: runbook hit rate > 90% (responders followed checklist steps), mean time to mitigation < 25 minutes for simulated Sev1.

Evidence collection checklist
----------------------------
- Attach: monitoring graphs (api-gateway, runtime-metrics, kv-cache), raw logs for first 60 minutes, config diff from last deploy, and any customer-reported artifacts.
- Tag artifacts with incident ID and store in incident bucket with ACL limited to responders and SRE leads.

Operational playbook links & references
--------------------------------------
- Runtime playbooks: confluence:eng-serving-runtime/runtime-incident-playbook (link)
- Model onboarding rollback guide: confluence:applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/rollback-guide (link)
- Status page publishing tool: docs/ops/status-cli (usage example included below)

Status CLI quick examples
------------------------
- Publish initial incident:
  ./status-cli create --id INC-2028-042 --status investigating --summary "Widespread inference errors in us-west" --update "Engineers investigating. Next update in 15m."
- Update follow-up:
  ./status-cli update --id INC-2028-042 --status "identifying_root_cause" --note "Traffic routed to warm pools; scaling in progress."

Change control after incident
----------------------------
- Any change that eliminates root cause must pass canary and benchmark suite before rollout: perf delta < 5% on P95 and cost delta evaluated.
- Document post-incident changes as a small PR with links to incident page and RCA.

Appendix: short checklists
-------------------------
- Bridge operator quick commands:
  - create bridge: bridgectl start --incident INC-2028-042 --owner <email>
  - add participant: bridgectl add --user <discord|slack|email>
- Evidence tags: tags: [INC-2028-042, sev1, runtime]

Owners and contact points
-------------------------
- On-call rotation: platform-oncall@redwood.com (Google Calendar and PagerDuty)
- Escalation: lider@redwood.com (Operations Lead)
- Customer Success escalation: cs-urgent@redwood.com
